 What seniors and families should know about Medicare Advantage and specialized plans for chronic conditions
 Published:  November 4, 2026 at 12:12 PM Tags:  wdiv , live in the d , zing health , medicare , annual enrollment , insurance , health The advertiser paid a fee to promote this sponsored article and may have influenced or authored the content.  Medicare’s Annual Enrollment Period is underway, giving seniors and people with certain disabilities an opportunity to review their health insurance coverage and explore options for 2027.
 The enrollment period runs through Dec. 7. During this time, beneficiaries can compare plans, evaluate changes to their existing coverage and determine whether their current plan meets their healthcare needs for the coming year.
 “Medicare can feel complicated,” said Garfield Collins of Zing Health. “This is when people can review their current coverage, see what is changing for 2027, and make sure they’re enrolled in a plan that fits their needs.”
 Medicare is the federal health insurance program for people 65 and older and certain younger individuals with qualifying disabilities. Beneficiaries generally choose between Original Medicare and Medicare Advantage plans.
 Original Medicare includes Part A, which covers hospital services, and Part B, which covers medical services. Prescription drug coverage is not included, so beneficiaries may need a separate Part D plan. While Original Medicare generally offers greater flexibility in choosing healthcare providers, out-of-pocket costs can be higher.
 Medicare Advantage plans, offered by private insurance companies, provide Part A and Part B coverage and typically include prescription drug benefits. Many also offer additional services, such as dental, vision, hearing, transportation and over-the-counter allowances.
 However, provider networks and covered services vary by plan, making it important for beneficiaries to confirm that their doctors, specialists, pharmacies and other healthcare providers are included.
 Another option for people with certain chronic conditions is a Chronic Condition Special Needs Plan, commonly known as a C-SNP. These specialized Medicare Advantage plans are designed for individuals with qualifying conditions, including diabetes, heart disease and chronic kidney disease.
 C-SNPs may offer more coordinated care, specialized provider support and resources tailored to managing specific health conditions.
 Collins said families helping aging parents or loved ones navigate Medicare should focus on two key considerations: coverage and value.
 “Make sure your doctors and specialists are in the plan’s network,” he said. “Review your prescriptions to ensure they’re covered, and confirm that the plan includes the services or treatments you expect to need next year.”
 For individuals managing chronic conditions, those considerations can be especially important. Families should also look at additional benefits, which may include transportation, grocery and utility allowances, wellness services and over-the-counter items.
 For people with chronic kidney disease or end-stage renal disease (ESRD), Collins said it is particularly important to understand how a plan handles ongoing treatment, dialysis appointments, specialist care and prescription coverage.
 At Zing Health, the focus is on helping beneficiaries understand their options and connect with healthcare resources, Collins said. Depending on the plan, members with qualifying chronic conditions may have access to care coordination, condition-management support and assistance navigating ongoing treatment.
 “Your health is our priority,” Collins said. “Our goal is to connect members with quality care, trusted doctors, specialists, benefits and resources that can help them manage their health effectively.”
 Medicare beneficiaries have until Dec. 7 to review their options and make changes for 2027. Before selecting a plan, experts recommend reviewing its specific benefits, costs, provider network, prescription coverage and eligibility requirements.
